name: Rack switch
kid: The switch on top of a tall cupboard of computers (a rack). It passes parcels to the computers in its own cupboard.
nerd: The top-of-rack (ToR) switch is a leaf: an uplink to every spine, and 25–100G down to the few dozen servers in its rack.

1995.kid: Drawn as today. In 1995 the web computer sat on a shelf, plugged into a hub with a thin copper cable.
1995.nerd: Drawn as today. In 1995 servers plugged into a shared 10BASE-T hub (10 Mbit/s, half duplex), not a 25G top-of-rack switch.
